why.cr_lev_1.m_nTotalStates: Training Medium gets the second state (static / pulsing / rotating, two of three per round) so that it prepares for the test (cr_lev_4: 2 forms × 2 colours × 2 states). Before, questions about the state (types 2 and 4, 40 % of questions) turned into «show all figures»: 60 % of Medium rounds were trivial, now 21 %. Tries per session: mean 20.5 → 17.6. up = 8000 stays reachable: no mistakes always give 12000; with a 10 % error rate per tap 89 % of sessions reach up (was 91 %).
why.cr_lev_2.m_nTotalStates: Training Hard gets the second state as well (2 forms × 2 colours × 2 states, like the test but 7–9 figures and 5 rounds). Trivial rounds 20 % → 0.3 %, tries per session 21.5 → 18.0. up = 13000 stays reachable: with a 10 % error rate per tap 69 % of sessions reach it (was 72 %); two mistakes pass in 82 % of sessions.
why.MG_color_rects_hard.level_up_param: up 14500 of 17000 → 18500 of 24000: the allowed share of wrong taps 8.2 → 12.7 % (two wrong taps in a session of 16 taps or more, before one). Average 9 → 22 % of games (target 20–30 %; median 107 → 43 games for the 10 steps), strong 68 → 87 % (target 75–90 %), novice 1 %. Games under down (7400): average 2 %, novice 29 %.
why.shell.b_mark_pnt_tables.102: Memorics (cr_lev_4, 6 rounds). The current table is lenient and compressed at the top: novice 48, average 74, strong 90 (54 % of attempts at 100), expert 93, so strong and expert are barely told apart. New marks: 25 / 53 / 79 / 87. The ceiling stays (a session without mistakes always gives 100: 38 % of strong attempts) because a session has only ≈ 18 taps; Memorics remains the noisiest game (SEM ≈ 20 points).
why.cr_lev_4.m_nShowCount: cr_lev_4 is used only by the test. 6 rounds instead of 4 give ≈ 18 taps instead of 12. Memorics has no time component: its mark is the count of wrong taps, and that count's luck is 90–98 % of the game's noise. The attempt-count luck (A = 4–25 taps per session) is only 3–8 % of the variance under per-tap and per-session error models alike, so a fixed price per mistake is not worth a code change (the SD of the mark falls by 3–6 % under per-session errors and grows by up to 11 % under per-tap errors). Cost ≈ +42 s for an average player. 8 rounds (+84 s) cut the Memorics SEM to ≈ 18 and the strong players' ceiling to 28 % (test_review.md §7).
why.cr_lev_0.m_nTotalForms: Easy gets two forms (2 forms × 2 colours, static). With one form three of the five question kinds (form, state, form + state) meant «show every figure», 60 % of the rounds, so Easy only asked where 3–5 figures were: every model player passed 100 % of games, and 82–93 % even if no wrong tap were allowed. With two forms such rounds are 20 % (Medium 21 %, Hard 0 %) and the ladder is regular: 4 / 6 / 8 kinds of figures on Easy / Medium / Hard. Wrong taps on Easy: novice 17 %, average 4 %, strong 3 % (memory model of tools/analysis/train_balance_memorics.mjs: capacity calibrated on the test level cr_lev_4 to 30 / 15 / 5 % wrong taps; real createRound and totalScore). cr_lev_0 is used only by training Easy.
why.cr_lev_0.MIN_OBJ_COUNT: Easy: 4–6 figures instead of 3–5 (Medium 5–7, Hard 7–9): 5 / 6 / 8 figures per round on the three levels. Together with the second form it makes Easy a real first step: wrong taps on Easy / Medium / Hard are 17 / 24 / 34 % for the novice (was 2 / 24 / 33 %) and 4 / 8 / 19 % for the average player (was 1 / 8 / 19 %).
why.cr_lev_0.MAX_OBJ_COUNT: Easy: 4–6 figures instead of 3–5, see cr_lev_0.MIN_OBJ_COUNT.
why.cr_lev_0.m_nShowCount: Easy: 4 rounds instead of 3 (Medium and Hard 5), about 12 taps per session instead of 10. With 3 rounds the pass rate jumps between «one wrong tap» and «none»; with 4 rounds the threshold 4700 holds the targets under other memory assumptions as well (novice 34–46 %, average 93–96 % for a memory cost weight of 0.3–0.8).
why.MG_color_rects_easy.in_app_ver_level_up_: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: easy — novice 60–75 % of games, average ≥ 95 %): up 4700 → 4000 of 6000: at most 18.5 % wrong taps (the score is the level cost × (1 − 1.8 × the share of wrong taps)), that is two wrong taps in a session of 11 taps or more (4700 allowed one, two in a long session). Novice 40 → 68 %, average 94 → 99 %, strong 99 %. The level is unchanged (4–6 figures, 2 forms × 2 colours, 4 rounds). Memorics is a starting game; unlock stays −1.
why.MG_color_rects_easy.level_up_param: Same threshold as in_app_ver_level_up_param (that one is read first).
why.MG_color_rects_med.level_up_param: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: medium — novice 35–45 % of games, average ≥ 85 %): up 10400 → 7500 of 12000: at most 20.8 % wrong taps — three in a session of 15 taps or more (the usual session has about 18), four in 20 or more (10400 allowed one; the original 8000 allowed three). Novice 3 → 42 %, average 56 → 97 %, strong 100 %; games for the 5 steps (median): novice 140 → 11, average 8 → 5. Real play logs agree (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md). The level and the Medium prices (shared with the test) are unchanged.
why.cr_game_wnd.g_nCRHardLevelCost: Hard level cost 17000 → 24000 (Easy 6000, Medium 12000; the test plays with the Medium prices and is not affected). On Hard the average player makes 19 % wrong taps (8 % on Medium) and each costs 1.8 taps, so he kept 65 % of the cost: mean 11140 against 10395 on Medium (1.07 ×), and the novice scored less on Hard than on Medium (6806 against 7053). With 24000 the mean rises on every step: novice 4394 / 7056 / 9505, average 5659 / 10349 / 15617 (Hard = 1.51 × Medium), strong 5754 / 11566 / 21285. The wrong-tap price stays 80 % of a tap.
